courses.title: Grammar I
skills_learned: explain types of Arabic sentences and word order therein
distinguish various types of Arabic tenses
analyse types of Mansbt and Marfct; and
to discover aspects of word case ending in Arabic sentences
courses.content_summary: Types of sentence in Arabic. Elements and factors in Arabic that affect the word order. Subjunctive word in Arabic (al-Mansbt and Appositives i.e. the Subject, Object of a sentence, `Ismu Inna and Khabaru Kna (at-Tawbc) for example: adjectives, affirmation, substitution and conjunction. Intensive study of the three Arabic tenses e.g. (Mdi Mudrc and `Amr)

courses.title: Language Drills I
skills_learned: read and comprehend Arabic texts
write short paragraphs
communicate and express himself in Arabic; and
demonstrate knowledge of Basic Arabic Grammar.
courses.content_summary: The course consolidates various aspects dealt with in ARA 101. It also entails extensive reading as well as comprehension exercises. Reading selected texts from poetry and prose. Answer questions about selected texts. Extensive exercises on writing short composition and summarizing texts.
learning_outcomes: read and comprehend Arabic texts
write short paragraphs
communicate and express himself in Arabic; and
demonstrate knowledge of Basic Arabic Grammar.

courses.title: Study Skills
skills_learned: analyse Arabic texts
read and summaries Arabic texts
demonstrate knowledge of note-taking ,
making notes from resources and use the library; 5. use Arabic dictionaries and correct his notes; and
writing word without spelling mistakes
courses.content_summary: Areas of reading, note-taking, note-making, Summarizing, using the library, the dictionary. Intensive exercise will be given for illustration and testing the level of comprehension. Intensive exercise on writing difficult Arabic words specially writing: (Hamzat alwasl, Hamzat alqatc, Hamzah in the middle and at the end of word) other areas to be studied are: ( Attā’ almarbutah and attā’ almaftūhah, Al-asshamsiyyah and al-alqamariyyah, ‘Alif almadd at the end of words).
courses.source_locator: Original CCMAS source: Arabic; ARA 103; Arts-CCMAS-2023-FINAL.pdf pp. 33, 34

courses.title: Introduction to Arabic Literature
skills_learned: analyse meanings, types and characteristics of literature
appreciate relevant Arabic literary works
identify types of Arabic literature
differentiate characteristics of Arabic literature in various eras; and
identify the various schools of thought in Arabic Literature.
courses.content_summary: Introduce students to the basic concepts of literature, with emphasis on the components (such as imagery and music), literary creation and literary appreciation, the divisions of Arabic Literature into literary periods, as well as the most outstanding characteristics of literary figures in each period. 200 Level GST 212 Philosophy, Logic And Human Existence (2 Units C: LH 30) Learning Outcomes A student who has successfully gone through this course should be able to: 1. explain the basic features of philosophy as an academic discipline; 2. identify the main branches of philosophy & the centrality of logic in philosophical discourse; 3. explain the elementary rules of reasoning; 4. distinguish between valid and invalid arguments; 5. think critically and assess arguments in texts, conversations and day-to-day discussions; 6. critically asses the rationality or otherwise of human conduct under different existential conditions;
learning_outcomes: analyse meanings, types and characteristics of literature
appreciate relevant Arabic literary works
identify types of Arabic literature
differentiate characteristics of Arabic literature in various eras; and
identify the various schools of thought in Arabic Literature.

courses.title: Entrepreneurship and Innovation
skills_learned: explain the concepts and theories of entrepreneurship, intrapreneurship, opportunity seeking, new value creation, and risk taking
state the characteristics of an entrepreneur
analyze the importance of micro and small businesses in wealth creation, employment, and financial independence
engage in entrepreneurial thinking
identify key elements in innovation
stages in enterprise formation, partnership and networking including business planning, and
describe contemporary entrepreneurial issues in Nigeria, Africa and the rest of the world
state the basic principles of e-commerce.
courses.content_summary: Concept of Entrepreneurship (Entrepreneurship, Intrapreneurship/Corporate Entrepreneurship,). Theories, Rationale and Relevance of Entrepreneurship (Schumpeterian and other perspectives, Risk-Taking, Necessity and opportunity-based entrepreneurship and Creative destruction). Characteristics of Entrepreneurs (Opportunity seeker, Risk taker, Natural and Nurtured, Problem solver and change agent, Innovator and creative thinker). Entrepreneurial thinking (Critical thinking, Reflective thinking, and Creative thinking). Innovation (Concept of innovation, Dimensions of innovation, Change and innovation, Knowledge and innovation). Enterprise formation, partnership and networking (Basics of Business Plan, Forms of business ownership, Business registration and Forming alliances and join ventures). Contemporary Entrepreneurship Issues (Knowledge, Skills and Technology, Intellectual property, Virtual office, Networking). Entrepreneurship in Nigeria (Biography of inspirational Entrepreneurs, Youth and women Entrepreneurship, Entrepreneurship support institutions, Youth enterprise networks and Environmental and cultural barriers to entrepreneurship). Basic principles of e-commerce.

courses.title: Digital Humanities: Application of Computer to the Arts
skills_learned: explain what Digital Humanities entails
appraise the DH techniques tools for data analysis
appreciate the importance of computers in the Humanities
apply DH to interdisciplinary research
appreciate the adoption of DH tools for entrepreneurship, and
apply DH to new research, publishing, media, networking.
courses.content_summary: Meaning of digital humanities. Interface between computing and the disciplines in the Arts. Methodological and interdisciplinary scope of digital humanities. Techniques of data analysis; application of Computer in the Arts disciplines; entrepreneurial, research, publishing, networking and application of various digital tools; and the new media.

courses.title: The Arts and Other Disciplines
skills_learned: appreciate the relationship between the Arts and other disciplines
distinguish between interdisciplinary, multidisciplinary and trans-disciplinary research
assess the interconnectivity between disciplines, and
engage in interdisciplinary, multidisciplinary and trans-disciplinary research.
courses.content_summary: Relationship between the Arts and other disciplines, e.g, Social Sciences, Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics, Medicine, etc. An investigation of the connection between the disciplines and the general intellectual terrain. Multidisciplinary, interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary interface of the Arts with other disciplines. Making connections across disciplines and perspectives.

courses.title: Grammar II
skills_learned: acquire knowledge of the evolution of Arabic grammar
identify some grammatical features related to nouns and verbs
analyse the Agent, the Vocative, Specification and Adverbs
identify subject and predicate in Arabic sentences; and
formulate dual and plural nouns from singular.
learning_outcomes: acquire knowledge of the evolution of Arabic grammar
identify some grammatical features related to nouns and verbs
analyse the Agent, the Vocative, Specification and Adverbs
identify subject and predicate in Arabic sentences; and
formulate dual and plural nouns from singular.

courses.title: Language Drills II
skills_learned: consolidate his ability to read and comprehend Arabic texts
acquire more knowledge of writing skills
improve his skills of note-taking; and
advance his ability to undertake independent search for knowledge in libraries and the internet.
courses.content_summary: : This course is designed to consolidate aspects dealt with in ARA 201. It is also designed for the acquisition of advanced reading and writing skills. Selected texts of poetry and prose are to be studied for comprehension and dictations. Using of physical and virtual libraries should be advanced in this course.
learning_outcomes: consolidate his ability to read and comprehend Arabic texts
acquire more knowledge of writing skills
improve his skills of note-taking; and
advance his ability to undertake independent search for knowledge in libraries and the internet.

courses.title: Texts from Pre-Islamic and Early Islamic Literature
skills_learned: study selected texts from pre and early Islamic literature
demonstrate knowledge of different types of literature in the period
identify distinctive contribution of Qur’ān to development of Arabic Language
identify contribution of Ḥadīth to development of Arabic Language; and
analyze texts from pre and early Islamic eras.
courses.content_summary: : A textual study of selections from such literary genres as poetry, proverbs, wise saying, folktales, soothsayers rhymed prose and sermons/ addresses. One of the ten famous preIslamic poems and another from the Islamic era should be studied, also one sermon from each of the two periods. Influence of Qur’ān and Ḥadīth on the development of Arabic Language should be emphasized.
learning_outcomes: study selected texts from pre and early Islamic literature
demonstrate knowledge of different types of literature in the period
identify distinctive contribution of Qur'n to development of Arabic Language
identify contribution of adth to development of Arabic Language; and
analyze texts from pre and early Islamic eras.

courses.title: Introduction to General Linguistics
skills_learned: acquire the basics of General Linguistics and its branches
identify components of General Linguistics
recognize the relationship between Linguistics and other fields of study; and
explore the efforts of the prominent scholars of this science in the Western world, and the contributions of traditional Arab linguists and their modern counterparts.
courses.content_summary: An introduction to the study of General Linguistics; definitions and its branches; the emergence and development of linguistics since the nineteenth century; efforts of its prominent scholars in the Western world; the contributions of traditional Arab linguists and the modern ones.
learning_outcomes: acquire the basics of General Linguistics and its branches
identify components of General Linguistics
recognize the relationship between Linguistics and other fields of study; and New Arts 37

skills_learned: explain detailed Arabic verbal morphological analysis
identify the rules of morphological analysis
analyze derivation and formation of word in Arabic Language; and
analyze naked and compound forms of words as well as the particles of augmentation in a detailed manner.
courses.content_summary: Definition and meaning of morphology. The morphological scale in Arabic language. And detailed analysis of Arabic verbal morphology; aspects of naked and compound forms of verbs as well as the particles of augmentation.
learning_outcomes: explain detailed Arabic verbal morphological analysis
identify the rules of morphological analysis
analyze derivation and formation of word in Arabic Language; and
analyze naked and compound forms of words as well as the particles of augmentation in a detailed manner.

courses.title: Arabic Literature in the Pre-Islamic & Early Islamic Periods
skills_learned: acquire general overview of the literature in pre and early Islamic Periods
study and analyse some short poems from the two periods; , and
to acquint himself/herself with notable literary figures from this period.
courses.content_summary: : General overview of the literature in the two periods, with some emphasis on the literary genres and figures; a detailed study of one of the seven odes; some short poems from such collections as Mufaddaliyyat, Hamāsah and Jamharah.
learning_outcomes: acquire general overview of the literature in pre and early Islamic Periods
study and analyse some short poems from the two periods; , and
to acquint himself/herself with notable literary figures from this period.

courses.title: Contemporary Arabic Prose
skills_learned: comprehend the meaning of modern terminologies and expressions as may be cited in selections from modern literary journals and daily press; 2. appreciate relevant Arabic literary works; and
identify types of modern Arabic prose
analyse the concepts of peace, conflict and security
list major forms, types and root causes of conflict and violence
differentiate between conflict and terrorism
enumerate security and peace building strategies
describe roles of international organisations, media and traditional institutions in peace building; and
differentiate the role of languages in peace and conflict resolution
courses.content_summary: Textual study of terminologies and expressions from modern Arabic literary works, journals and daily press; Arabic TV channels for modern Arabic expressions. To study distinctive modern Arabic prose and the influence of present Arabic dialects on modern Arabic prose. Contribution of the social media and technology in general in advancing Arabic language. 300 Level GST 312- Peace and Conflict Resol

courses.title: Research Methods in the Arts
skills_learned: explain the meaning, usefulness and characteristics of research methods
enumerate the types and approaches to research in the Arts
identify the essential variables in research methods, such as research problem, formulation of objectives, sampling techniques, among other
engage in field works to collect data
formulate good research proposal
conduct original research / Long essay at the final year; and
write a report of the Long essay/research project, devoid of plagiarism and other ethical issues.
courses.content_summary: Meaning and characteristics of research; research methods; types of research in the Arts disciplines. Approaches to research, problems, proposals, techniques of data collection. Analysis and interpretation. Criteria for determining good data and the use of library resources; archives, internet, audio visual aids, field work, interviews, questionnaires, observations and focused-group techniques. Research reports, report writing, language of academic reports, organisation, originality of research; authenticity, ethical issues, plagiarism, documentation, editing, etc.

courses.title: Grammar IV
skills_learned: attain understanding of certain grammatical features such as Numbers
differentiate types of Arabic pronouns, types of declension; and
develop the ability to analyse Intensification of Imperfect and Inflection of Defective Verbs.
courses.content_summary: : The study of certain grammatical features such Numbers, Pronouns, types of declension, the Jussive Mood, Verbs of Approximation, Intensification of Imperfect and Inflection of Defective Verbs.

courses.title: Semantics
skills_learned: explain the meaning of semantics, its concept and development
identify the efforts of Arabic linguists in ancient and modern times in area of semantics studies
develop the ability to analyse and discover some types of semantics in Arabic language
explain the relationship between signifier signified
appreciate aspects of multiplicity of meanings, such as synonymy, antonym
identify elements of semantic fields; and
state the characteristics of taboo.
courses.content_summary: Introduce the concept of semantics and its development over time; the efforts of Arabic linguists in ancient and modern; the relationship between signifier and signified; the differences between language and speech; the types of semantics development, its factors and features; aspects of multiplicity of meanings, such as synonymy, antonym and linguistic taboo.
learning_outcomes: explain the meaning of semantics, its concept and development
identify the efforts of Arabic linguists in ancient and modern times in area of semantics studies
develop the ability to analyse and discover some types of semantics in Arabic language
explain the relationship between signifier signified
appreciate aspects of multiplicity of meanings, such as synonymy, antonym
identify elements of semantic fields; and
state the characteristics of taboo.

courses.title: Introduction to Classical Arabic Criticism
skills_learned: identify the historical evolution and development of Arabic classical criticism
identify early efforts of scholars on Arabic criticism
recognize methods of early critics; and
criticize texts according to rules of Arabic Classical Criticism
courses.content_summary: Basic approach to Classical Arabic literary criticism and a survey of the development of Classical Arabic Criticism, laying special emphasis on AL-`midi's Muwzanah.

courses.title: The Novel I
skills_learned: explain the definition and History of the novel in Arabic
discover components of the novel, and
attain ability to study and analyse the Arabic novel.
courses.content_summary: : The definitions of the novel, History of the novel in Arabic; the study and analysis of a specific novel. To study in general the main elements of novel i.e. narration, plot, theme, setting and character and to apply them on the selected novel of the study.
learning_outcomes: explain the definition and History of the novel in Arabic
discover components of the novel, and
attain ability to study and analyse the Arabic novel.

courses.title: A Play I
skills_learned: identify the definition and History of a play in Arabic Literature
discover characteristics of a play
attain ability to study and analyse an Arabic play; and
discover components of play.
courses.content_summary: : The course entails definition of and History of play and the Arabic art performance in Arabic; characteristics and components of a play; the analysis a play in Arabic literature. The course includes the study of types of play and elements of play: Role and character, relationships, situation, voice, movement, focus, tension, space, time, language, symbol, audience, mood and atmosphere. And to apply these elements on the selected play of study.
learning_outcomes: identify the definition and History of a play in Arabic Literature
discover characteristics of a play
attain ability to study and analyse an Arabic play; and
discover components of play.

courses.title: Rhetoric I
skills_learned: explain a short historical survey of Arabic Rhetoric

appreciate elements of Aeabic Rhetoric such as Similes, Metaphors of Arabic; 3. identify the three components of Arabic rhetoric i.e. (Albayān Badīc and Almacānī); and 4. analyse components of Arabic rhetoric in a selected text.
courses.content_summary: A short historical survey of Arabic Rhetoric, the "Bayn" and "Macn" Similes, Metaphors, `Ijz, Itnb, Isnd and Wal. The course includes the study of some founders of Arabic Rhetoric i.e. al-Jiz in his book albayn wa at-tabyin, Arrummni in his book Annawdir, Albqiln, Aljurjn, as-Sakkki and alqazwin.
learning_outcomes: explain a short historical survey of Arabic Rhetoric; New Arts 42
courses.source_locator: Original CCMAS source: Arabic; ARA 316; Arts-CCMAS-2023-FINAL.pdf pp. 42, 43

courses.title: Prosody 1
skills_learned: expain the historical background to Arabic Prosody
identify the metres of prosody and their features in Arabic
identify efforts of Khalīl bin Ahmad on Arabic prosody, and
analyse Arabic poetry.
courses.content_summary: Historical background of Arabic Prosody, “Ziḥāfāt” and “cIlāl” i.e. deviations and irregularities in Arabic metres of poetry. The Study and Analysis of the fourteen metres. Detailed study of the founding father of Arabic prosody: Alkhalīl bin Ahmad. Applied study of the metres of poetry on selected poems, the selection should include poetry of some Nigerian poets.
learning_outcomes: expain the historical background to Arabic Prosody
identify the metres of prosody and their features in Arabic
identify efforts of Khall bin Ahmad on Arabic prosody, and
analyse Arabic poetry.

courses.title: Phonetics and Phonology
skills_learned: analyse the branches of phonetics and phonology of the Arabic Language
pronounce Arabic sounds correctly
identify aspects as morphemes, allomorphs, phonemes, as well as the sound system of Arabic Language; and
demonstrate knowledge of the language lab and its benefits in the study of sounds.
courses.content_summary: : Introduce the study of branches of phonetics i.e. Articulatory, Acoustic and Auditory phonetics and the study of phonology of the Arabic Language; consonant and vowels, morphemes, allomorphs, phonemes, as well as the sound system of Arabic. The Arabic Language Lab should be used to demonstrate Arabic sounds and pronunciation.
learning_outcomes: analyse the branches of phonetics and phonology of the Arabic Language
pronounce Arabic sounds correctly
identify aspects as morphemes, allomorphs, phonemes, as well as the sound system of Arabic Language; and
demonstrate knowledge of the language lab and its benefits in the study of sounds.

courses.title: Translation I
skills_learned: identify history and basic principles of translation
analyse qualifications of a translator
explain the steps of translation
types of translation; and
translate simple texts from and into Arabic
courses.content_summary: Introduce the students to the history and basic principles of translation. qualifications of a translator. Steps of translation. types of translation, and technicalities of translation in relation to Arabic and English languages. The importance of dictionaries in translation. Conduct intensive exercises in literary translation from and to Arabic.

courses.title: Methods of Research
skills_learned: identify the rules of academic research in Arabic studies
acquire ability to design and carry out research and present an original piece of writing in the discipline
undertake independent research work without supervision; and
identify the scientific methods of editing Arabic manuscripts.
courses.content_summary: Expose special Honours students the modern methods of research in Arabic Studies, relationship between the student and his supervisor, the role of each one of them, how to write a research proposal, authentication of research resources and exposing them to publishing a research. To draw the attention of students to the danger of plagiarism and the scientific methods of editing Arabic manuscripts.
learning_outcomes: identify the rules of academic research in Arabic studies
acquire ability to design and carry out research and present an original piece of writing in the discipline
undertake independent research work without supervision; and
identify the scientific methods of editing Arabic manuscripts.

courses.title: Comparative Arabic Literature
skills_learned: define comparative literature, its development and establishment in Arabic studies
compare Arabic literature with others
study and analyse the influence of Arabic on other literary traditions
influence of other literary traditions on Arabic; and
identify influence of Arabic literature on Nigerian literary traditions in local languages.
courses.content_summary: Development of comparative literature and its establishment in Arabic studies; basic ideas in comparative literature such as Arabic-Western Literary elations, the influence of Arabic on other literary traditions, translation theory, thematology, Literature and Religion, Literature and the other Arts.
learning_outcomes: define comparative literature, its development and establishment in Arabic studies
compare Arabic literature with others
study and analyse the influence of Arabic on other literary traditions
influence of other literary traditions on Arabic; and
identify influence of Arabic literature on Nigerian literary traditions in local languages.

courses.title: Information and Communication Technology for Arabic
skills_learned: operate Arabic oriented computer hardware and software
use World Wide Web resources on Arabic language and literature and other Library potentials of the internet for Arabic studies as well as other ICT resources helpful in Arabic studies research; and
operate computer for his personal benefit
courses.content_summary: This course is to introduce student to components of computer, office productivity software, understanding spreadsheets, word processing, presentations and understanding databases. Arabic oriented computer hardware and software feature; survey of World Wide Web resources on Arabic language and literature; Library potential of the internet for Arabic studies as well as other ICT resources helpful in Arabic studies. 400 Level
learning_outcomes: operate Arabic oriented computer hardware and software
use World Wide Web resources on Arabic language and literature and other Library potentials of the internet for Arabic studies as well as other ICT resources helpful in Arabic studies research; and
operate computer for his personal benefit.

courses.title: Grammar V
skills_learned: develop critical approaches to traditional Arabic Grammar
analyze the debate between the call for easing Arabic grammar and those who oppose this motion
explain the evolution of Grammar Schools in Arabic; and
be exposed to some selected topics of Arabic Grammar, such as the Construct, the Appositives, exception.
courses.content_summary: : The study of Schools of Arabic Grammar and their evolution in Kufa, Basra, Bagdad, Eygpt and Andalus. Modern critical approaches to traditional Arabic Grammar as contained in such works as Ibrahim Mustafa’s ‘Iḥyā’ an-Nahw, Makhazūmi’s an-Nahw al-caArabī:Naqdun waTawjīhun and Ibn Madha’s Ar-Radd calā al-Nuḥāt; selected topics of Arabic Grammar, such as the Construct, the Appositives, Exception, the Adverb of Condition, and the Theory of the Agent, the Vocative, the Verbs of Wonderment, the Verbs of Pre-eminence and Nominatives.
learning_outcomes: develop critical approaches to traditional Arabic Grammar
analyze the debate between the call for easing Arabic grammar and those who oppose this motion
explain the evolution of Grammar Schools in Arabic; and
be exposed to some selected topics of Arabic Grammar, such as the Construct, the Appositives, exception.

courses.title: The Writings of Nigerian Ulama
skills_learned: explain the history and development of Arabic in Nigeria
identify the influence of Magrib on Nigerian Arabic
selected topics and texts from works of Nigerian authors in Arabic Language; and
be familiar with works of some notable Nigerian Arabists.
courses.content_summary: Brief history of the advent of Arabic language into Nigeria; textual study of selected literary works of Nigerian authors such as Usman B. Fodio, Abdullahi B. Fodio, Muhammad Bello, Wazir Junaid and Abubakar Atiq for analysis, appreciation and comparison with similar works in the Arab World.
learning_outcomes: explain the history and development of Arabic in Nigeria
identify the influence of Magrib on Nigerian Arabic; New Arts 45

courses.title: Modern Arabic Poetry
skills_learned: be familiar with development of major modern schools of poetry
identify the contribution Arabs in diaspora to modern Arabic poetry; and
be exposed to Arabic poetry.
courses.content_summary: : Advanced survey of the development of major modern schools of poetry and their representative selections. Contribution of Arabs in diaspora to modern Arabic poetry. The influence of European poetry on Arabic modern poetry. To study works of some poets like: Nazār Qabāni, Badr shākir Assayyāb, Nāzik Al-malāikah, Mahmūd Darwīsh, Jibrān Khalīl Jibrān etc.
learning_outcomes: be familiar with development of major modern schools of poetry
identify the contribution Arabs in diaspora to modern Arabic poetry; and
be exposed to Arabic poetry.

courses.title: Modern Arabic Prose
skills_learned: identify the development of major modern schools of prose
identify the influence, of translation on modern Arabic prose
discuss advantage and disadvantage of present mass- media on modern Arabic prose; and
be exposed to representative selections of modern Arabic prose.
courses.content_summary: : Survey of the growth and development of modern Arabic prose; representative selections from the works of novelists, playwrights and essayists. Influence of translation on modern Arabic prose. Advantage and disadvantage of present mass- media on modern Arabic prose should be studied in this course.
learning_outcomes: identify the development of major modern schools of prose
identify the influence, of translation on modern Arabic prose
discuss advantage and disadvantage of present mass- media on modern Arabic prose; and
be exposed to representative selections of modern Arabic prose.

courses.title: Selected Topics in Arabic Grammar
skills_learned: develop critical approach to Arabic grammar, and
analyse various views of scholars on Arabic grammar
criticize the call for substituting classical Arabic with Modern Arabic dialects; 4. explain the views of those who call for easing Arabic grammar and the contrary; and
courses.content_summary: Selected topics in Arabic Grammar; Views of Ibn Madha' Alqrtub, Ahmad `Amn, Shawq Daif, and their call for easing Arabic grammar should be studied. Also views of other scholars who insist on sticking to traditional grammar are to be surveyed. The call for substituting classical Arabic with Modern Arabic dialects, advantages and disadvantages to be discussed.
learning_outcomes: develop critical approach to Arabic grammar, and
analyse various views of scholars on Arabic grammar; New Arts 46
courses.source_locator: Original CCMAS source: Arabic; ARA 410; Arts-CCMAS-2023-FINAL.pdf pp. 46, 47

courses.title: Introduction to Arabic Lexicography
skills_learned: explain the historical background to the development of Arabic Lexicography
appreciate types of Arabic dictionary; and
use and analyse different types of dictionaries.
courses.content_summary: Historical background to the development of Arabic Lexicography, through different periods of time, the Schools of the Arabic Lexicon; the study of some old and modern dictionaries, according to order of lexicons entries i.e. the phonetic order, the last letter order and the alphabetic order. Also to be studied is the Language Academies and their efforts in development of Arabic dictionaries. Some defects of old dictionaries and the aspiration to complete the big historical Arabic dictionary.
learning_outcomes: explain the historical background to the development of Arabic Lexicography
appreciate types of Arabic dictionary; and
use and analyse different types of dictionaries.

courses.title: Rhetoric II
skills_learned: analyse advance areas of Arabic rhetoric
discuss new ideas and approaches to Arabic Rhetoric
discover Jurjān’s theory of Nadhm in his two books “Addalā’il wa Al-‘asrār”; and
analayse relationship between rhetoric and semantic and other sciences.
courses.content_summary: : The study of the “Badīc’” Aspect of Arabic Rhetoric as (Jinās, Sajac, Tibāq, Muqābala, Tawriyah, Ḥusnu taclīl and Mubālagah) as well as discussions on new ideas or approaches to Arabic and Rhetoric.
learning_outcomes: analyse advance areas of Arabic rhetoric
discuss new ideas and approaches to Arabic Rhetoric
discover Jurjn's theory of Nadhm in his two books "Addal'il wa Al-`asrr"; and
analayse relationship between rhetoric and semantic and other sciences.

courses.title: Applied Linguistics
skills_learned: identify the basics of Applied Linguistics, including error analysis and contrastive analyses
discuss modern ideas and approaches to teaching of Arabic language as second language, and
analyze difficulties expected to face native language speaker when learning Arabic.
courses.content_summary: Introduction to the concept of applied linguistics, the science of error analysis and contrastive Analyses; The importance of applied linguistics in Arabic studies and its teaching as a second language, and recent innovations in this field, efforts of notable scholars in Applied Linguistics and contributions of some major centres of teaching Arabic to non- speakers in Arab world i.e. University of Cairo, Ummul Qura University in Saudi Arabia, Institute of Arabic Language at Khartoum Sudan, and others.

courses.title: Translation II
skills_learned: acquire ability to advanced types of translation, and
use and edit machine translation.
courses.content_summary: Advanced types of translation from and into Arabic. intensive exercises include using and editing machine translation.
learning_outcomes: acquire ability to advanced types of translation, and
use and edit machine translation.

courses.title: Entrepreneurship for Arabic
skills_learned: discover available chances for Arabic graduate in government, private sector, and
secure self-employment by opening his Arabic school
design and start business related to Arabic in computer, commerce, teaching; and
master the arts of Arabic calligraphy and translation.
courses.content_summary: This will provide a wide survey of chances for Arabic graduate and avail him to available vacancies, in government, private sector and self-employment. These include foreign affairs, journalism, Arabic computer typesetting, teaching, translation and interpretation. Training the student on Arabic calligraphy and other art works dependent on Arabic language expertise, i.e. writing Quranic verses.
learning_outcomes: discover available chances for Arabic graduate in government, private sector, and
secure self-employment by opening his Arabic school
design and start business related to Arabic in computer, commerce, teaching; and
master the arts of Arabic calligraphy and translation.

programmes.name: Archaeology

courses.title: Introduction to Archaeology
skills_learned: have knowledge of what archaeology is and its aims
explain the origins of archaeology as a discipline and its eurocentric roots. understand how archaeologists discover sites, recover and handle archaeological evidence; and
identify the different dating methods used in archaeology, the principles behind each of the methods and their limitations in archaeological interpretation.
courses.content_summary: The meaning of archaeology and its basic aims. Origin and growth of archaeology as a discipline with particular reference to Africa. Principles and techniques of archaeology. Site prospection in archaeology. Dating methods in archaeology. Archaeology and development.

courses.title: Introduction to Human Origins
skills_learned: expain the different perspectives in the study of human origins
identify the difference between the creation theory and the theory of evolution
appreciate the fossil record and how it supports the study of human origins; and
analyse the gaps in our current knowledge on human origins.
courses.content_summary: : Theories of human origin (the creation theory and the theory of evolution). Charles Darwin and the theory of evolution. The fossil record with particular reference to Africa (Australopithecines to Homo sapiens) Genetics, molecular biology and human origins. The cognitive revolution.

courses.title: A survey of Old World Archaeology
skills_learned: explain the major themes in the archaeology of the old world
explain the history of human dispersal across the old world
clearly explain the different food systems up to the neolithic revolution; and
articulate the significance of the neolithic revolution in the old world.
courses.content_summary: : A survey of old world geography and paleo ecology. Prehistory from proto-culture through the Stone Age to the ‘Neolithic Revolution’. The primary and secondary dispersal of humans in the old world. Major civilizations of the old world. Energy capture in the old world. ARC 104 African Indigenous Knowledge (3 Units C: LH 45)

courses.title: Introduction to Anthropology
skills_learned: analyse the meaning and scope of anthropology
explain basic theories and methods in anthropology
articulate the interface between archaeology and anthropology; and
explain the challenges of doing anthropology in Africa.
courses.content_summary: New Arts                        59 Nature and scope of Anthropology. Culture and Change in human societies. Four sub fields of anthropology (Archaeology, linguistic anthropology, physical anthropology and socio cultural anthropology) Field methods in anthropology. Ethical issues in anthropology. The challenges of doing anthropology in Africa. 200 Level GST 212 Philosophy, Logic and Human Existence

courses.title: Digital Humanities: Application of Computer to the Arts
skills_learned: explain what Digital Humanities entails
appraise the DH techniques tools for data analysis
appreciate the importance of computers in the Humanities
apply DH to interdisciplinary research
appreciate the adoption of DH tools for entrepreneurship; and
apply DH to new research, publishing, media, networking.
courses.content_summary: Meaning of digital humanities. interface between computing and the disciplines in the Arts. Methodological and interdisciplinary scope of digital humanities. Techniques of data analysis. Application of Computer in the Arts disciplines. Entrepreneurial, research, publishing, networking and application of various digital tools. The new media.

courses.title: The Arts and Other Disciplines
skills_learned: appreciate the relationship between the arts and other disciplines
distinguish between interdisciplinary, multidisciplinary and trans-disciplinary research
assess the interconnectivity between disciplines; and
engage in interdisciplinary, multidisciplinary and trans-disciplinary research.
courses.content_summary: New Arts             61 Relationship between the Arts and other disciplines e.g, Social Sciences, Science, Technology Engineering, Mathematics, Medicine, etc. An investigation of the connection between the disciplines and the general intellectual terrain. Multidisciplinary, interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary interface of the Arts with other disciplines. Making connections across disciplines a

courses.title: A survey of New World Archaeology
skills_learned: identify the different stages of archaeological development in the new world and characterise each
articulate the evidence for food production in the new world and argue in what ways, it differs from similar evidence in the old world
identify and characterise the major civilizations of the new world and argue how and why they collapsed; and
understand the extent to which the environment played a major role in the rise and collapse of civilizations in the new word.
courses.content_summary: A survey of New world geography and paleo ecology. The peopling of the New world. The different stages of cultural development in the New world ( the lithic, archaic, formative, classic and post classic). Food production in the New world. Civilizations of the New world. Energy capture in the New world.

courses.title: Archaeology of Africa
skills_learned: clearly argue out how africa is the cradle of humankind
analyse how agriculture and metallurgy led to the development of complex societies in africa
identify the significance of the nile valley, east and southern africa in the archaeology of the continent; and
explain the bantu problematic and the different lines of inquiry used in bantu studies.
courses.content_summary: The African paleo environment. Language families in Africa. Africa and human origins. Stone Age cultures of Africa. Food production in Africa. Egypt and the Nile valley. The African Iron Age and Bantu migrations.

courses.title: Theory of Archaeology l
skills_learned: define archaeology, its goals and the nature of its evidence
explain the history of archaeology, when and how it emerged as a scientific discipline
articulate site formation processes and how these affect preservation of archaeological data; and
know the different theories and models of explanation in archaeology
courses.content_summary: The nature of archaeological evidence. How archaeological sites are formed. The history of archaeology and how it became a modern science. Archaeological theories and models of explanation including the 3 Age system, diffusion, migration and invention. The culture history approach. Culture ecology. Systems theory and ethno archaeology. Ownership and stewardship of archaeological resources. Ethical challenges in archaeology.
courses.source_locator: Original CCMAS source: Archaeology; ARC 203; Arts-CCMAS-2023-FINAL.pdf pp. 62, 63

courses.title: Quaternary Studies and Archaeology
skills_learned: learnt and known the significance of the quaternary as a geological epoch
knowledge of how the quaternary sciences have in the understanding and interpretation of archaeological data
knowledge to distinguish the two epochs of the quaternary and argue how the evidence from the pleistocene has enhanced our understanding of human evolution; and
arguments on how the quaternary offers an interdisciplinary window in the study of the environment.
courses.content_summary: The Quaternary as a geological time period. Basics of Quaternary archaeology. Pleistocene and Holocene environments and their impact on our physical environment, eco systems, climate and culture. Quaternary sciences and human origins.
learning_outcomes: learnt and known the significance of the quaternary as a geological epoch
knowledge of how the quaternary sciences have in the understanding and interpretation of archaeological data
knowledge to distinguish the two epochs of the quaternary and argue how the evidence from the pleistocene has enhanced our understanding of human evolution; and
arguments on how the quaternary offers an interdisciplinary window in the study of the environment.

courses.title: Field Archaeology
skills_learned: analyse the theoretical basis of archaeological survey as it relates to the discovery of sites, and surface collections
document and collect surface finds, process, study and analyse them
carry out a traverse survey using the prismatic compass and gps; and
produce a site map and write a publishable site report.
courses.content_summary: : The course is both theoretical and practical covering the following topics: Laws, ethics and safety in field archaeology. Survey and reconnaissance techniques in archaeology. Surface collection techniques. Field photography and illustrations. Elementary use of survey equipment. Map reading and map making. Excavation techniques. Stratigraphic profiles and the Harris Matrix.

courses.title: Science in Archaeology
skills_learned: identify the significance of the physical and life sciences in the study of archaeological resources;
argue how micro and macro organisms affect the preservation of archaeological remains
identification and recovery of fauna and flora remains in the archaeological context; and
analyse different ways science has helped archaeological survey and the discovery of sites New Arts  64
courses.content_summary: Contributions of the physical and life sciences to the development of archaeology Site prospection, scientific handling and analysis of data. Dating methods and interpretation. Stratigraphy. Ecology and the Systems theory. Laboratory analysis (pottery and stone analysis). Basics of geoarchaeology, zooarchaeology, archaeogenetics and archaeometry. Laboratory analysis.

courses.title: Entrepreneurship: Contract Archaeology
skills_learned: design and conduct a cultural impact assessment
design and conduct an environmental impact assessment; and
report an archaeological investigation.
courses.content_summary: : Basics of contract archaeology. Cultural impact assessment. Environmental impact assessment. Rescue archaeology. Stakeholder analyses. Field work safety issues and ethics. Budgets and resource mobilization. 300 Level GST 312- Peace and Conflict Resolution (2 Units C: LH 30) Learning Outcomes At the end of the course, students should be able to: 1. analyse the concepts of peace, conflict and security; 2. list major forms, types and root causes of conflict and violence; 3. differentiate between conflict and terrorism; 4. enumerate security and peace building strategies; and 5. describe roles of international organisations, media and traditional institutions in peace building Course Contents Concepts of peace, conflict and security in a multi-ethnic nation. Types and theories of conflicts: ethnic, religious, economic, geo-political conflicts. Structural conflict theory, realist theory of conflict, frustration-aggression conflict theory. Root causes of conflict and violence in Africa: indigene and settlers phenomena; boundary/boarder disputes; political disputes; ethnic disputes and rivalries. Economic inequalities; social dispute. Nationalist movements and agitations. Selected conflict case studies – Tiv-Junkun; Zango Kartaf. Chieftaincy and land disputes, etc. Peace building, management of conflicts and security. Peace and human development. Approaches to eace & conflict management --- (religious, government, community leaders etc.). elements of peace studies and conflict resolution. Conflict dynamics assessment scales. Constructive and destructive, justice and legal framework. Concepts of social justice; the Nigerian legal system. Insurgency and terrorism. Peace mediation and peace keeping. Peace and Security Council (international, national and local levels). Agents of conflict resolution – conventions, treaties, community policing. evolution and imperatives.

programmes.name: African Tradition Religion

courses.title: Introducing African Traditional Religion
skills_learned: define African Traditional Religion
deal with conceptual ambiguities ; and
recognise the contributions of scholars to the development of the discipline.
courses.content_summary: Introduction to the main features of the African traditional religion. Problems of definition of African Traditional Religion. Status of African Traditional Religion as a world religion. Conceptual clarifications: African Traditional or African Indigenous Religion(s). African Traditional Religions, African Traditional Religion, African Religion (Afrel). Historical development of African Traditional Religion as an academic discipline. Contributions of Geoffrey Parrinder, J.S. Mbiti, E.B. Idowu, J.O. Awolalu, and so on.

courses.title: Survey of African Traditional Religion
skills_learned: debate the bias against the religion
appreciate the resilience of ATR; and
learn the structure of belief across the African continent.
courses.content_summary: Further definitions of African Traditional Religion. Western perceptions of African Traditional Religion. Derogatory terminologies used by Western scholars to describe African Traditional Religion. African scholars’ reactions to the derogatory terms. African peoples from the East, West, South and North conception of African Traditional Religion. The pyramid of African belief: Belief in God, divinities, spirits, ancestors, medicine personnel.

courses.title: Ancestorship in African Traditional Religion
skills_learned: appreciate that there is life after death
explain that not all those who died can become ancestors
learn the conditions for ancestor status
appreciate the roles of ancestors in African community; and
determine the influence of Christianity and Islam on belief in ancestorship
courses.content_summary: Definition of ancestors. Ancestors as the living-dead. Ancestor-hood as salvation in African Traditional Religion. Traditional qualifications for ancestorship in different cultural contexts. Influence of Christianity and Islam on the concept of ancestorship. Reassessment of the criteria of becoming an ancestor in modern Africa. Modernity and claim of abandonment of ancestors. Revival of ancestral cults in Africa.
courses.source_locator: Original CCMAS source: African Tradition Religion; ATR 103; Arts-CCMAS-2023-FINAL.pdf pp. 80, 81

courses.title: African Traditional Religion and Culture
skills_learned: appreciate the relationship between religion and culture
demonstrate how African culture influenced political system; and
realise the dynamics of culture in Africa’s development.
courses.content_summary: Definition and clarification of culture. Correlation between African Traditional Religion and cultures. Culture, African Traditional Religion, and Identity. Culture, African Traditional Religion and rites of passage. African Traditional Religion and culture contact. African Traditional Religion and political system such as monarchy, military regimes, democracy within African religious and cultural context. Belief in ritual practices to influence political processes. African culture and socio-economic development. Power relations within the traditional religious sphere. African Traditional Religion, culture and corruption in Africa. 200 Level GST 212 Philosophy, Logic and Human Existence (2 Units C: LH 30) Learning Outcomes A student who has successfully gone through this course should be able to: 1. explain the basic features of philosophy as an academic discipline; 2. identify the main branches of philosophy & the centrality of logic in philosophical discourse; 3. analyse the elementary rules of reasoning; 4. distinguish between valid and invalid arguments; 5. think critically and assess arguments in texts, conversations and day-to-day discussions; 6. critically asses the rationality or otherwise of human conduct under different existential conditions; 7. develop the capacity to extrapolate and deploy expertise in logic to other areas of knowledge, and 8. guide his or her actions, using the knowledge and expertise acquired in philosophy and logic. Course Contents

courses.title: Entrepreneurship and Innovation
skills_learned: explain the concepts and theories of entrepreneurship, intrapreneurship, opportunity seeking, new value creation, and risk taking
state the characteristics of an entrepreneur
analyze the importance of micro and small businesses in wealth creation, employment, and financial independence
engage in entrepreneurial thinking
identify key elements in innovation
describe stages in enterprise formation, partnership and networking including business planning
describe contemporary entrepreneurial issues in Nigeria, Africa and the rest of the world, and
state the basic principles of e-commerce.
courses.content_summary: Concept of entrepreneurship (entrepreneurship, intrapreneurship/corporate entrepreneurship,). theories, rationale and relevance of entrepreneurship (schumpeterian and other perspectives, risk-taking, necessity and opportunity-based entrepreneurship and creative destruction). Characteristics of entrepreneurs (opportunity seeker, risk taker, natural and nurtured, problem solver and change agent, innovator and creative thinker). Entrepreneurial thinking (critical thinking, reflective thinking, and creative thinking). Innovation (concept of innovation, dimensions of innovation, change and innovation, knowledge and innovation). Enterprise formation, partnership and networking (basics of business plan, forms of business ownership, business registration and forming alliances and joint ventures). Contemporary entrepreneurship issues (knowledge, skills and technology, intellectual property, virtual office, networking). Entrepreneurship in nigeria (biography of inspirational entrepreneurs, youth and women entrepreneurship, entrepreneurship support institutions, youth enterprise networks and environmental and cultural barriers to entrepreneurship). Basic principles of e-commerce.

appraise the DH techniques tools for data analysis New Arts 82
appreciate the importance of computers in the Humanities
apply DH to interdisciplinary research
appreciate the adoption of DH tools for entrepreneurship
apply DH to new research, publishing, media, networking

courses.title: The Arts and Other Disciplines
skills_learned: appreciate the relationship between the Arts and other disciplines
distinguish between interdisciplinary, multidisciplinary and trans-disciplinary research
assess the interconnectivity between disciplines, and
engage in interdisciplinary, multidisciplinary and trans-disciplinary research.
courses.content_summary: Relationship between the Arts and other disciplines, e.g, Social Sciences, Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics, Medicine, etc. Investigation of the connection between the Arts disciplines and the general intellectual terrain. Multidisciplinary, interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary interface of the Arts with other disciplines. Making connections across disciplines and perspectives.

courses.title: General Introduction to t he Study of Religion
skills_learned: be familiar with the evolution of the concept of religion
appreciate the problems of defining religion; and
learn the different approaches such as: sociological, philosophical, ethical, Phenomenological, psychological, and so on
courses.content_summary: Etymologies, definitions, and theories of the origins of religion. Approaches to the study of religion. Purposes and difficulties encountered in the study of religion. Theories and methods of studying religion: phenomenological, comparative, ethnographical, grounded theology, Marxian, Weberian, anthropological, sociological, historical, psychological, literary, philosophical, economic, and so on.

courses.title: Intersection of ATR with Christianity and Islam
skills_learned: determine the level of intersectionality
assess the infusion of religious beliefs
understand how religions enhance human flourishing
appreciate different cosmological resources defining African religioscape
courses.content_summary: Definitions of religious intersectionality. Approaches to religious intersectionality. Critique of religious intersectionality. Aspects of ATR appropriated by Christianity and Islam: vigil, invocation and curses as prayers, traditional marriage/Christian/Islamic, traditional burial/Christian/Islamic, engaging cosmological resources for human flourishing, ProtoAncestor concept.

courses.title: Contemporary Worship in ATR
skills_learned: appreciate how ATR has re-defined itself
assess the influence of culture contact; and
assess the contextualisation of borrowed format.
courses.content_summary: Engaging the concept of worship. Object(s) of worship in African Traditional Religion. Precolonial structure of worship in African Traditional Religion. Organised worship in ATR such as in Arousa temple in Benin City, Ijo Orunmila among the Yoruba and so on which are structured in form of orthodox churches. Liturgical order of worship. Move of the spirit. Worship and divination, revelation or prophecy. Worship, music and dance of worship. On site visit could be arranged where it is possible, and students should write their report for assessment.

courses.title: African Concept of the Family
skills_learned: define the composition and nature of the African family system
appreciate the significance of African family; and
appreciate the resilience of African family system .
courses.content_summary: Definitions of family. African concept of family. Importance of marriage in Africa. Types and nature of family. Functions of family system. Challenges of contemporary African family. The place of first son or daughter in the family. Western influence on African family system. Resilience of African family system. Authority and hierarchy in African family system. Family, inheritance, and succession.

courses.title: Entrepreneurship in ATR
skills_learned: appreciate the traditional entrepreneurial skills and mode of acquisition
practically create cultural, aesthetic and economic value; and
pursue a thriving entrepreneurship outfit.
courses.content_summary: Definitions of entrepreneurship. Importance of entrepreneurship. African traditional entrepreneurial skills and acquisition. Entrepreneurship and traditional art works, their symbolism and significance, their aesthetic and economic value; different cultural emblems, artifacts; cultural and royal paraphernalia and so forth. Setting up shop for sale of art works and other traditional gift items. 300 Level GST 312- Peace and Conflict Resolution (2 Units C: LH 30) Learning Outcomes At the end of the course, students should be able to: 1. analyse the concepts of peace, conflict and security; 2. list major forms, types and root causes of conflict and violence; 3. differentiate between conflict and terrorism; 4. enumerate security and peace building strategies; and 5. describe roles of international organisations, media and traditional institutions in peace building. Course Contents Concepts of peace, conflict and security in a multi-ethnic nation. Types and theories of conflicts: ethnic, religious, economic, geo-political conflicts. Structural conflict theory, realist theory of conflict, frustration-aggression conflict theory. Root causes of conflict and violence in Africa: indigene and settlers phenomena; boundary/boarder disputes; political disputes; ethnic disputes and rivalries. Economic inequalities; social dispute. Nationalist movements and agitations. Selected conflict case studies – Tiv-Junkun; Zango Kartaf. Chieftaincy and land disputes, etc. Peace building, management of conflicts and security. Peace and human development. Approaches to eace & conflict management --- (religious, government, community leaders etc.). elements of peace studies and conflict resolution. Conflict dynamics assessment scales. Constructive and destructive, justice and legal framework. Concepts of social justice; the Nigerian legal system. Insurgency and terrorism. Peace mediation and peace keeping. Peace and Security Council (international, national and local levels). Agents of conflict resolution – conventions, treaties, community policing. evolution and imperatives. Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR). Dialogue, arbitration, negotiation, collaboration, etc.

enumerate the types and approaches to research in the Arts
identify the essential variables in research methods, such as research problem, formulation of objectives, sampling techniques, among other
identify the essential variables in reformulating good research proposal
conduct original research / Long essay at the final year; and
write a report of the Long essay/ research project devoid of plagiarism and other ethical issues.
courses.content_summary: Meaning and characteristics of research; research methods. Types of research in the Arts disciplines. Approaches to research, problems, proposals, techniques of data collection, analysis and interpretation. Criteria for determining good data and the use of library resources, archives, internet, audio visual aids, field work, interviews, questionnaires, observations and focused-group techniques. Research reports, report writing, language of academic reports, organisation, originality of research, authenticity, ethical issues, plagiarism, documentation, editing, etc.
learning_outcomes: explain the meaning, usefulness and characteristics of research methods; New Arts 86
courses.source_locator: Original CCMAS source: African Tradition Religion; FAC 301; Arts-CCMAS-2023-FINAL.pdf pp. 86, 87

courses.title: Theory in the Humanities
skills_learned: capture complexity by means of a single general statement
systematically think from principles through application to conclusions
analyse complex data to minimal units
make out underlying patterns in art phenomena, and
utilize evidence to organize and explain complex phenomena in the humanities.
courses.content_summary: In-depth analyses of the diversity of theories employed by researchers in the arts and humanities; social integrative theory, gender theory, inter-culturality theory, liberation theory, etc.; theoretical underpinnings as the essential foundation of humanities scholarship; evaluation of the merits of scholarly works.

courses.title: The Spirit World of the African
skills_learned: appreciate the existence of spirits
distinguish between malignant and ancestor spirits
draw the hierarchy of the different spirits; and
appreciate their intervention in human and community affairs.
courses.content_summary: This spirit world of the African. Spirit forces in African worldview. Cosmic forces such as witches, (the Bwanga, Nyame), the apparitions/phantoms, as well as the witch doctor. Divinities in selected ethnic groups. Good and malignant spirits. Witchcraft from African and western perspectives. The spirits as agents and agencies in human society. Reality of the spirit in contemporary society.

courses.title: African Traditional Religion and the Environment
skills_learned: possess knowledge of the relationship between religion and environment
appreciate the need to care for the environment; and
apply African environmental ethics to environmental issues.
courses.content_summary: General conceptions of the environment. African conception of the environment. African cosmos as composite. Myths and sacrality of the environment. African Traditional Religion, natural and built environment. Forces in the African environment. Totems and preservation of the ecosystem. Reverence for the cosmos and consequences of desecration. A comparative analysis of the environment in pre- and post-colonial Africa. The place and role of African environmental ethics in the preservation of the environment.

courses.title: ATR and Globalisation
skills_learned: demonstrate the concepts of globalisation
appreciate the advantages and disadvantages of globalisation
influence of globalisation on African religion and culture; and
debate local-global responses to globalisation.
courses.content_summary: Definitions and conceptualisation of globalisation. What is globalisation? African Traditional Religion in a Globalised world. Effects of globalisation and its media on African Traditional Religion and culture. How globalisation is affecting African culture and orientation and also being affected by the latter. Contributions of African culture to global culture: communality, human dignity, respect and honour, shame culture and so on. History and influence of Nollywood on African religion and culture. Selected movies can be analysed.

courses.title: Introducing African Indigenous Knowledge System
skills_learned: conceptualise AIKS
appreciate the contribution of African to the body of knowledge; and
apply to critical discourse on at a global level.
courses.content_summary: Definitions of indigenous knowledge systems. African indigenous knowledge system. African Traditional Religion and Indigenous Knowledge Systems. Sources of AIKS: proverbs, folklores, myths, cosmologies, rituals, and the epistemologies derived from them. Application of AIKS in modern society. Challenges and production of AIKS in a globalised world.
courses.source_locator: Original CCMAS source: African Tradition Religion; ATR 304; Arts-CCMAS-2023-FINAL.pdf pp. 88, 89

courses.title: Introducing African Herbal Medicine
skills_learned: identify leaves and determine their medicinal values
process some of the leaves; and
suggest ways to tackle the challenge of standardisation.
courses.content_summary: Definition and nature of African medicine. Medicine and magic in African Traditional Religion. African herbal medicine as prophylaxis. African traditional prognosis. Potent word or incantation in herbal medicine. Identifying different leaves for herbal purposes; determining their medicinal values; and processing. Dealing with the problem of measurement and dosage. The growing market for traditional medicine. Measures for standardisation, preservation and economic benefits for personal and national development.

courses.title: Long Essay
skills_learned: deploy the knowledge he has gained during the programme into research; and
contribute to knowledge in a little way.
courses.content_summary: The student undertakes a research of about 5,000 words on an approved topic by the Department, wherein he clearly engages methodological and theoretical approaches. He also follows the approved reference style used by the Department.

courses.title: ATR and the Africa Diaspora
skills_learned: appreciate the history of Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade
demonstrate the transposability of African Traditional Religion; and
assess the unintended consequences of globalising ATR
courses.content_summary: A brief history of the Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade. External and internal factors responsible for Slave Trade. Roles of individuals and organisations involved in the Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade. Cost and consequences of Slave Trade on Africa. The transposability and establishment of African Traditional Religion in the New World. The practice and flourishing of ATR in Cuba, Brazil, Portugal, and the US.
courses.source_locator: Exact course content cross-checked against the NUC CCMAS PDF; removed extracted page header 'Arts 89                                                                         New' after course ATR 401.

courses.title: The Supreme Being in African Tradition
skills_learned: learn the names and attributes of God in different African communities
demonstrate the nature of God; and
realise the place of God in African worldview
courses.content_summary: Multiple conceptions of God in African ethnic and regional groups. Examples from West, East, Central and Southern Africa. The concept of God as polytheism, deism, monotheism, animism in African Traditional Religion. Mbiti, Parrinder, Idowu, Awolalu’s etc. views of the concept of God in Africa and contemporary decolonial viewpoints. The attributes of the God in Africa. The problem of evil from African Traditional Religion’s worldview.

courses.title: Traditional Medicine in Nigeria/Africa
skills_learned: learn about the healer
learn the protocols of healing
differentiate between medicine and magic; and
determine the efficacy of traditional medicine.
courses.content_summary: Practical rudiments of traditional/alternative healing. Mystification and demystification of traditional healing processes. Excursion to such places as Pax-Herbal Laboratories in Ewu, Edo State (or any other identified/recognised herbal home nearest to the university) to understudy trado-medicine and its economic/business value. The students are to submit individual or group report on their excursion. Traditional medicine personnel and response to epidemic or pandemic such as Ebola, COVID-19 and so on.

courses.title: African Traditional Religion and Contemporary Issues
skills_learned: assess the ambivalence of religion in contemporary Nigeria
relate African Traditional Religion to other contemporary issues; and
tease out ways of locally combating contemporary menaces.
courses.content_summary: African Traditional Religion and food and food security. Poverty and development from the perspective of African Traditional Religion. African Traditional Religion and politics, economy. African Traditional Religion and aesthetics. African Traditional Religion and human dignity, human rights, respect for human life in the face of increasing rate of human rituals and kidnapping. African Traditional Religion and terrorism. African Traditional Religion and leadership. African Traditional Religion and modern science. African Traditional Religion and secularity.
courses.source_locator: Original CCMAS source: African Tradition Religion; ATR 404; Arts-CCMAS-2023-FINAL.pdf pp. 90, 91

courses.title: ATR and Gender Relations
skills_learned: trace the history of the development of gender in Africa
explore the underlying role of African Traditional Religion in gender construct; and
assess the challenges that globalisation poses to gender issues in Africa
courses.content_summary: Traditional African conception of gender. African Traditional Religion and patriarchy, matriarchy. African Traditional Religion and homosexuality. LGBTI and African Traditional Religion. African Traditional Religion and heterosexuality and so on. Specific relations of gender in different African cultural settings. Roles of gender in the family and community. Contemporary debate in African gender construct.

courses.title: ATR and the Nigerian Nation
skills_learned: assess the contributions of ATR to national development
assess the neglect of traditional values in national development
proffer viable solutions to the challenges
courses.content_summary: African notions of nation and nation-building. Roles of African Traditional Religion in national development: ATR, non-violence and peace. ATR and national politics. Utilisation of ATR resources for political development. ATR and sports. ATR and the Nigerian economy. ATR and social value. Debate on oath-taking and corruption in Nigeria. Public holidays, religious ecumenism, Nigerian Inter-religious Council, and the status of ATR in Nigeria’s secularity.

courses.title: ATR and the Pluralistic World
skills_learned: engage the concept of pluralism
contribute to the debate; and
appraise how the debate affects Nigeria.
courses.content_summary: Concept and nature of pluralism. Religious pluralism and religious plurality. ATR and Nigerian religious pluralism. Contributions of ATR to religious tolerance; religious dialogue. ATR and African palaver. ATR and alternative dispute resolution. courses.title: Elementary Chinese I                           2 Units C: LH 30
skills_learned: acquire a basic understanding of chinese language and culture
cultivate the skills of elementary chinese listening and speaking; and
acquire a basic understanding of Chinese character recognition and writing
courses.content_summary: The first half of a two-semester Mandarin Chinese course that aims to help beginners develop communicative competence in the basic four skills (listening, speaking, reading and writing) and culture of Chinese. Aimed at introducing the basic knowledge of Chinese phonetics, vocabulary, grammar and characters.

Pronunciations are given precise hint, methods are equally provided to correct mistakes. Designed for improving practice at the same time, on the basis of correct writing and pronunciation, and creates room for further improvement.

It also embraces listening to audio materials drawn from short passages.

apply advanced grammatical structures, including descriptive complements, that support communication at the intermediate level of proficiency; and
compose longer descriptive, narrative, and expository pieces

It enhances the studests' listening, speaking, writing and hearing abilities to better communicate with Chinese natives about most topics on an intermediate level. This includes the understanding of general topics and non-specialist contents to able to be able to communicate with native speakers about similar topics.

skills_learned: use speaking and listening skills to converse with ease and confidence about routine tasks and social situations;
read and compose colloquial text using chinese characters
apply wider cultural knowledge and recognize chinese cultural values in order to interact with native speakers of mandarin chinese with elevated appropriateness; and
take the step from intermediate to advanced level Chinese
courses.content_summary: A continuation of Chinese 201. Building upon language skills acquired in the previous course, Chinese 202 will increase students' knowledge of the fundamental grammatical structures of Chinese and their ability to communicate in both spoken and written Chinese in a wide range of situations in daily, social and academic life. Students will be introduced to reading materials of increasing complexity on a variety of topics reflecting different aspects of traditional and modern Chinese culture.

skills_learned: tell the basic rules of translation and interpretation
translate documents from english to chinese and vice versa; and
interpret meanings from English to Chinese and vice versa
courses.content_summary: Aims at introducing some foreign language translation theories, especially Chinese-English translation theory, by taking many practices of Chinese-English oral interpretation and written translation, to deepen students' understanding of foreign language translation theory and improve ability of Chinese-English translation, in order to fit the needs of future work.

courses.title: Research Methodology                                       2 Units C: LH
skills_learned: devise a complete and rich research methodology
collect, process, and analyse research data; and
write a good thesis or an article that could be published
courses.content_summary: Introduces key research methodologies such as induction and deduction, analysis and synthesis, quantitative and qualitative research, investigation method, experimental method etc., to improve students' abilities in applying multiple methods in research and to pave a strong foundation for Project (Thesis) writing.

courses.title: Introduction to Chinese Grammar   2 Units C: LH 30
skills_learned: tell the basic grammatical rules and sentence elements in chinese
use the basic chinese sentence patterns and structures that are error free; and
observe the unique nature of chinese grammar grammatical sentences that are error free in Chinese.
courses.content_summary: Introduces Chinese grammar by focusing on the elementary grammatical points such as parts of speeches, the basic sentence patterns and structures, so as to be able to produce grammatical sentences that are error free in Chinese.

courses.title: Introduction to Chinese Literature  2 Units C: LH 30
skills_learned: appreciate the literary works of ancient, contemporary and modern China
identify the norms and culture of ancient, contemporary and modern China through the literary works;
denote the prominent literary figures of ancient, contemporary and modern China
observe the literary rules and skills of ancient, contemporary and modern China
courses.content_summary: Theoretical elements of Chinese literature- drama, poetry, and prose, glimpses of the ancient, contemporary and modern Chinese literature. The mystery in remote times, the Poetry in Tang Dynasty, the Ci Poetry in Song Dynasty, and the novel in Ming & Qing Dynasty and the fiction of modern times.

courses.title: Entrepreneurial skills in Chinese Studies 2 Units C: LH 30
skills_learned: command the chinese language skills and knowledge of the chinese culture from their prior studies, and begin to explore and identify the traits of entrepreneurship and to create their entrepreneurial profile not only in the chinese language, but also in the appropriate cultural context and format;
identify the business norm and practice of the chinese entrepreneurs, how the chinese society perceives these entrepreneurs;

create an entrepreneurial personal profile in a culturally appropriate way that includes a western and chinese resume featuring their personality traits, background, personal experiences and abilities, and other desirable qualities of entrepreneurs; and
participate in chinese job search sites as well as entrepreneurship websites in a chinesespeaking country.
courses.content_summary: Prepares students with the foundational knowledge of entrepreneurship to be career-ready by developing the linguistic and cultural competencies in Chinese, as well as the critical thinking skills necessary to successfully collaborate and compete in today’s entrepreneurial global business context. It integrates technology, cultural awareness, real-world business practice, and the fundamental linguistic competencies derived from the interpretive, interpersonal and presentational communication modes framework for World Language learning. These include developing of students' listening, reading, writing, speaking, and critical thinking skills within a culturally appropriate entrepreneurial context. Students will write narrative, and expository essays, including argument analysis and complete research projects within a business framework utilizing an expected level of Chinese language structure, accuracy, and fluency.

courses.title: Chinese Civilisation           2 Units C: LH 30
skills_learned: discuss the dynasties of ancient china, and the monarchs of these dynasties; 2 explain the contributions of ancient chinese civilizations to global civilization; and
discuss the prominent individuals and events throughout Chinese history
courses.content_summary: Introduces to the origin and development of ancient civilization of China. Three Emperors and Five Sovereigns of remote antiquity, Xia and Shang Dynasty, Zhou Dynasty, Spring-Autumn and Warring States Period, Qin and Han Dynasty, Wei-Jin-Northern and Southern Dynasty, Sui and Tang Dynasty, Song Dynasty, Yuan Dynasty, Ming and Qing Dynasty. 300 Level                               (2 Units C: LH 30)

courses.title: Peace and Conflict Resolution
skills_learned: analyse the concepts of peace, conflict and security
list major forms, types and root causes of conflict and violence
differentiate between conflict and terrorism
enumerate security and peace building strategies; and
describe roles of international organisations, media and traditional institutions in peace building.
courses.content_summary: Concepts of peace, conflict and security in a multi-ethnic nation. Types and theories of conflicts: ethnic, religious, economic, geo-political conflicts. Structural conflict theory, realist theory of conflict, frustration-aggression conflict theory. Root causes of conflict and violence in Africa: indigene and settlers phenomena; boundary/boarder disputes; political disputes; ethnic disputes and rivalries. Economic inequalities; social dispute. Nationalist movements and agitations. Selected conflict case studies – Tiv-Junkun; Zango Kartaf. Chieftaincy and land disputes, etc. Peace building, management of conflicts and security. Peace and human development. Approaches to eace & conflict management --- (religious, government, community leaders etc.). elements of peace studies and conflict resolution. Conflict dynamics assessment scales. Constructive and destructive, justice and legal framework. Concepts of social justice; the Nigerian legal system. Insurgency and terrorism. Peace mediation and peace keeping. Peace and Security Council (international, national and local levels). Agents of conflict resolution – conventions, treaties, community policing. evolution and imperatives. Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR). Dialogue, arbitration, negotiation, collaboration, etc. Roles of international organizations in conflict resolution - (a). the United Nations (UN) and its conflict resolution organs; the African Union and Peace Security Council. ECOWAS in peace keeping. The media and traditional institutions in peace building. Managing post-conflict situations; refugees. Internally Displaced Persons (IDPS). The role of NGOs in post-conflict situations.
